mechanism_narrative: RETAIL_REC has risen each of the last three weeks (-32.9 to -30.7), indicating an established recovery momentum that will continue linearly over the next four weeks, producing a higher 28-day mean than the prior 28 days.
evidence_refs: fact:RETAIL_REC improved from -32.9 to -30.7 over three consecutive weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC fails to improve further or reverses direction in the next 2-3 weekly readings despite the prior three-week upward trend.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp jump in PARKS mobility (9.3 to 26.7 over three weeks) signals substitution of outdoor leisure for indoor retail and recreation trips, which will suppress RETAIL_REC growth over the following two weeks if the surge persists above threshold.
candidate_trigger: PARKS rises by more than 15 points over a two-week window and stays above the prior baseline
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS rose from 9.3 to 26.7 across the snapshot weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC continues to rise or remains flat in the two weeks following a PARKS surge exceeding the 15-point threshold.

mechanism_narrative: TRANSIT remains deeply suppressed (around -41 to -44) across all four weeks, indicating persistent restrictions on movement or commuting that will continue to cap RETAIL_REC recovery over the next four weeks under a tightened-restrictions regime.
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT stayed between -44.4 and -41.3 and WORKPLACES between -32.6 and -31.6 across all four weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises substantially over the next four weeks even though TRANSIT and WORKPLACES remain depressed near current levels, disproving the restriction-cap mechanism.

mechanism_narrative: When both TRANSIT and WORKPLACES remain simultaneously deeply negative, their joint suppression of commuting-linked foot traffic compounds to hold RETAIL_REC flat or declining over the next two weeks, more strongly than either series alone would predict.
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT at -41.3 and WORKPLACES at -32.6 in the most recent week, both near four-week lows
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC improves over the next two weeks despite TRANSIT and WORKPLACES both remaining below -30, indicating no compounding suppression effect.

mechanism_narrative: GROCERY_PHARM's narrowing negative gap (-4.4 to -2.4) signals a broader normalization of essential-trip behavior that, once it crosses into positive territory, will precede a similar normalization in RETAIL_REC within one week.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM crosses above 0 percent change from baseline
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM improved steadily from -4.4 to -2.4 across the four weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not rise in the week following GROCERY_PHARM's crossing above zero, or GROCERY_PHARM never crosses zero within the observation horizon.

mechanism_narrative: The strong rise in PARKS mobility reflects a seasonal shift toward favorable outdoor weather that draws discretionary trips away from retail venues, depressing RETAIL_REC over the next two weeks during the warm-season period.
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS values remain elevated (19.9 to 26.7) over the last two weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises in tandem with continued high PARKS readings, indicating no seasonal substitution effect.

mechanism_narrative: RESIDENTIAL mobility remains persistently elevated (9.0 to 10.1) across all four weeks, indicating sustained stay-at-home guidance or norms that will continue to suppress RETAIL_REC recovery over the next four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL stayed between 9.0 and 10.1 across all four weeks with no downward trend
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises significantly over the next four weeks even though RESIDENTIAL remains at or above 9.0, contradicting the suppression mechanism.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous improving trend in both RETAIL_REC and TRANSIT over the last three weeks reflects a reinforcing mobility-recovery feedback loop where easier transit access enables more retail trips, which in turn sustains transit use, predicting continued joint improvement within one week.
evidence_refs: fact:both RETAIL_REC (-32.9 to -30.7) and TRANSIT (-44.4 to -41.3) improved concurrently over the snapshot weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC and TRANSIT diverge in the next week, with one improving while the other stagnates or declines, breaking the reinforcing loop assumption.
